_meta.source: Curated clinically significant pairwise interactions between drugs in the QuickRx NLEM-2022 formulary. Class groups keep the rule list maintainable; '@GROUP' in a rule expands to every member. Severity: 'major' = avoid/needs strong justification, 'moderate' = use with caution/monitor.
_meta.disclaimer: Decision support only — not a substitute for clinical judgment or a full interaction database.

rules.note: Greatly increased bleeding risk — NSAIDs impair platelets and can potentiate warfarin.
This antimicrobial potentiates warfarin — expect INR rise and bleeding risk; monitor closely.
Rifampicin induces warfarin metabolism — anticoagulation may fail; INR monitoring essential.
Dual anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy — high bleeding risk unless specifically indicated.
Duplicate NSAID therapy — additive GI-bleed and renal risk with no added benefit.
NSAIDs reduce methotrexate clearance — risk of methotrexate toxicity.
Both are folate antagonists — risk of severe bone-marrow suppression.
Hyperkalaemia risk — monitor serum potassium.
Reduced lithium clearance — risk of lithium toxicity; monitor levels.
Raises digoxin levels — risk of digoxin toxicity; reduce digoxin dose and monitor.
Additive AV-node blockade — risk of severe bradycardia and heart block.
Additive QT prolongation — risk of torsades de pointes.
Both prolong QT — combined use increases arrhythmia risk.
CYP3A4 inhibition raises domperidone levels — QT prolongation risk.
Additive QT prolongation.
Serotonin syndrome risk and lowered seizure threshold.
Additive serotonergic effect — watch for serotonin syndrome.
Serotonin syndrome risk — counsel the patient on warning symptoms.
SSRIs impair platelet function — added GI bleeding risk with NSAIDs; consider gastroprotection.
CYP3A4 inhibition raises statin levels — risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis; pause or switch statin.
Raises carbamazepine levels — toxicity risk (ataxia, drowsiness).
May raise phenytoin levels — monitor for toxicity.
Reduced theophylline clearance — narrow therapeutic window, toxicity risk.
Iron/calcium/antacids chelate this drug and block absorption — separate doses by 2–4 hours.
Omeprazole/esomeprazole reduce clopidogrel activation — prefer pantoprazole.
Added GI bleeding risk.
Added risk of peptic ulcer and GI bleeding — consider gastroprotection.
Contraindicated — profound hypotension when PDE5 inhibitors combine with nitrates.
Potentiated sulfonylurea effect — risk of severe hypoglycaemia.
Reduced colchicine clearance — risk of life-threatening colchicine toxicity.
Additive CNS and respiratory depression.
Dopamine antagonist opposes levodopa — worsens parkinsonism; prefer domperidone.
